words: إن ربك هو يفصل بينهم يوم القيمة
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God adjudicates at the Resurrection, distinguishing truth from falsehood by distinguishing the right from the wrong; their disagreement concerned religion.
rows.anchor: يقضي فيميز الحق من الباطل بتمييز المحق من المبطل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conjunction coordinates with an omitted clause of the same kind, and the subject is inferred from what follows.
rows.anchor: الواو للعطف على منوي من جنس المعطوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The walkers past the destroyed generations’ dwellings are the people of Mecca, passing them during trade journeys.
rows.anchor: يعني أهل مكة يمرون في متاجرهم على ديارهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reads يمشون with a doubled shīn.
rows.anchor: { يمشون فى مسكنهم } يعني أهل مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hearing here means reflective listening and taking admonition.
rows.anchor: أفلا يسمعون } سماع تدبر واتعاظ.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The land is one whose vegetation has been cut away, not land that never grows, since God brings crops from it.
rows.anchor: التي جرز نباتها أي قطع وأزيل لا التي لا تنبت

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view takes al-jarz as a place in Yemen.
rows.anchor: وقيل اسم موضع باليمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Vegetation feeds livestock, such as figs and foliage, while people eat grain and fruit.
rows.anchor: من الزرع. { أنعمهم } كالتين والورق. { وأنفسهم } كالحب والثمر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Crops should make people recognize God’s complete power and bounty.
rows.anchor: فيستدلون به على كمال قدرته وفضله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remember God abundantly through most times and every kind of remembrance due Him: glorifying, praising, declaring oneness, and magnifying Him.
rows.anchor: يغلب الأوقات ويعم الأنواع بما هو أهله من التقديس والتحميد والتهليل والتمجيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: David’s favor was either superiority over other prophets, as following gifts show, or all people, including prophethood, scripture, kingship, and beautiful voice.
rows.anchor: أي على سائر الأنبياء وهو ما ذكر بعد، أو على سائر الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountains return praise with David or lament over sin; God may create his voice in them, or contemplation may move them to praise.
rows.anchor: رجعي معه التسبيح أو النوحة على الذنب، وذلك إما بخلق صوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another sense is that the mountains accompany David wherever he travels.
rows.anchor: أو سيري معه حيث سار.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant from awb means return to praise whenever David repeats it; parsed as apposition to “favor” or “We gave,” with an implied “We said.”
rows.anchor: وقرىء «أوبي» من الأوب أي ارجعي في التسبيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Birds may coordinate with the mountains by syntax, with “favor,” or be an accusative accompaniment to “return”; nominative coordinates with the mountains’ expressed case.
rows.anchor: عطف على محل الجبال ويؤيده القراءة بالرفع عطفا على لفظها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nominative reading coordinates birds with the mountains’ expressed ending, treating the inherent ending as inflection.
rows.anchor: القراءة بالرفع عطفا على لفظها تشبيها للحركة البنائية العارضة بالحركة الإعرابية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording portrays mountains and birds as rational beings obeying David, magnifying his stature and God’s dominion.
rows.anchor: لما فيه من الفخامة والدلالة على عظم شأنه وكبرياء سلطانه، حيث جعل الجبال والطيور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made iron pliable in David’s hand like wax, shapeable without heating or hammering, through softening or strength.
rows.anchor: جعلناه في يده كالشمع يصرفه كيف يشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God commanded David to make the coats; أن may be explanatory or infinitive.
rows.anchor: أمرناه أن اعمل ف { أن } مفسرة أو مصدرية.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are broad coats of mail; a variant reads صابغات, and David was the first to make them.
rows.anchor: دروعا واسعات، وقرىء «صابغات» وهو أول من اتخذها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: David should regulate the weaving so the mail rings fit proportionately.
rows.anchor: وقدّر في نسجها بحيث يتناسب حلقها، أو قدّر مساميرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A view regulates rivets so they are neither thin and loose nor thick and splitting; Bayḍāwī rejects it because David’s mail was not riveted.
rows.anchor: ورد بأن دروعه لم تكن مسمرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural command addresses David and his household.
rows.anchor: الضمير فيه لداود وأهله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sees what they do and will reward them.
rows.anchor: إني بما تعملون بصير } فأجازيكم عليه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God subjected the wind to Solomon.
rows.anchor: أي وسخرنا له الريح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant makes al-rīḥ nominative, “the wind is subjected”; another reads plural al-riyāḥ.
rows.anchor: وقرىء { الريح } بالرفع أي ولسليمان الريح مسخرة وقرىء «الرياح».

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wind traveled a month’s journey in the morning and another month’s journey in the evening.
rows.anchor: جريها بالغداة مسيرة شهر وبالعشي كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Variants read غدوتها and روحتها.
rows.anchor: وبالعشي كذلك، وقرىء «غدوتها» «وروحتها».

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Molten copper flowed from a Yemeni source like water from a spring, hence it is called a spring.
rows.anchor: النحاس المذاب أساله له من معدنه فنبع منه

words: ومن الجن من يعمل بين يديه
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The jinn clause may coordinate with wind, with “of the jinn” fronted circumstantially, or be an independent clause.
rows.anchor: عطف على { الريح } { ومن الجن } حال مقدمة، أو جملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The jinn worked by Solomon’s Lord’s command.
rows.anchor: { بإذن ربه } بأمره. { ومن يزغ منهم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever deviates from obedience to Solomon is threatened with the afterlife Fire.
rows.anchor: ومن يعدل منهم. { عن أمرنا } عما أمرناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant uses the causative form أزاغه.
rows.anchor: وقرىء { يزغ } من أزاغه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threatened punishment is the Fire of the afterlife.
rows.anchor: نذقه من عذاب السعير } عذاب الآخرة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Blind and seeing represent unbeliever and believer; another view makes them an idol and God.
rows.anchor: الكافر والمؤمن، وقيل هما مثلان للصنم ولله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Darkness and light represent falsehood and truth.
rows.anchor: ولا الباطل ولا الحق.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shade and the scorching wind represent reward and punishment.
rows.anchor: ولا الثواب ولا العقاب،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating “nor” on both sides reinforces the denial that opposites are equal.
rows.anchor: ولا لتأكيد نفي الاستواء وتكريرها على الشقين لمزيد التأكيد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ḥarūr derives from heat and denotes simoom; alternatively, simoom blows by day and ḥarūr by night.
rows.anchor: فعول من الحر غلب على السموم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative distinguishes daytime simoom from nighttime ḥarūr.
rows.anchor: وقيل السموم ما يهب نهارا والحرور ما تهب ليلا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Living and dead again represent believers and unbelievers, a stronger comparison hence repeated verb; alternatively, scholars and ignorant people.
rows.anchor: تمثيل آخر للمؤمنين والكافرين أبلغ من الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God enables whomever He wills to understand His signs and take admonition.
rows.anchor: هدايته فيوفقه لفهم آياته والاتعاظ بعظاته.

words: وما أنت بمسمع من في القبور
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling persistent unbelievers dead extends the metaphor and tells the Prophet to give up hope of making them hear.
rows.anchor: ترشيح لتمثيل المصرين على الكفر بالأموات ومبالغة في إقناطه عنهم.

words: ومن الناس والدواب والأنعام مختلف ألوانه كذلك
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People, animals, and livestock vary in color just as fruits and mountains do.
rows.anchor: ألونه كذلك } كاختلاف الثمار والجبال.

words: إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only scholars truly fear God: fear requires knowledge of the one feared and His attributes and acts, so greater knowledge brings greater fear.
rows.anchor: إذ شرط الخشية معرفة المخشي والعلم بصفاته وأفعاله

words: إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء
rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: The Prophet says he is the most God-fearing and mindful of God among them, illustrating the link between knowledge and fear.
rows.anchor: " إني أخشاكم لله وأتقاكم له "

words: إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bayḍāwī follows the statement about fear with God’s acts as evidence of His complete power.
rows.anchor: ولذلك أتبعه بذكر أفعاله الدالة على كمال قدرته،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Putting God before the scholars as subject restricts who fears; reversing order reverses emphasis.
rows.anchor: وتقديم المفعول لأن المقصود حصر الفاعلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reads God in the nominative and “scholars” in the accusative, taking fear metaphorically as reverence that inspires awe.
rows.anchor: وقرىء برفع اسم الله ونصب العلماء على أن الخشية مستعارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s might and forgiveness explain fear: He punishes persisting tyrants and forgives the repentant.
rows.anchor: تعليل لوجوب الخشية لدلالته على أنه معاقب للمصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They persist in reciting the Qur’an or following it until it marks them; alternatively, God’s Book means all scriptures, praising later believers.
rows.anchor: يداومون على قرائته أو متابعة ما فيه حتى صارت سمة لهم وعنوانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They give as circumstances permit; alternatively, secret giving is voluntary and public giving obligatory.
rows.anchor: وقيل السر في المسنونة والعلانية في المفروضة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The trade is reward sought through obedience; the phrase is the predicate of إن.
rows.anchor: تحصيل ثواب الطاعة وهو خبر إن.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The trade will neither stagnate nor perish in loss; this phrase qualifies it.
rows.anchor: لن تكسد ولن تهلك بالخسران صفة للتجارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The removed sorrow is fear of the outcome, livelihood hardship and misfortunes, or Satan’s whispering and similar distress.
rows.anchor: همهم من خوف العاقبة، أو همهم من أجل المعاش وآفاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant vocalizes the word al-ḥuzn.
rows.anchor: وقرىء { الحزن }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God forgives sinners and appreciates the obedient.
rows.anchor: للمذنبين. { شكور } للمطيعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dār al-muqāma is the abode of lasting residence; entry is by grace, since God owes no one a reward.
rows.anchor: من إنعامه وتفضله إذ لا واجب عليه

words: لا يمسنا فيها نصب ولا يمسنا فيها لغوب
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no toil or weariness in Paradise because there are no duties or strenuous work; denying weariness after toil intensifies the point.
rows.anchor: ولا كد، أتبع نفي النصب نفي ما يتبعه مبالغة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No second death is decreed for unbelievers, so they cannot gain release by dying.
rows.anchor: لا يحكم عليهم بموت ثان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The subjunctive “so they die” has an implied أن.
rows.anchor: فيموتوا } فيتسريحوا، ونصبه بإضمار أن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reads the verb in the indicative, coordinated with “is decreed.”
rows.anchor: وقرىء «فيموتون» عطفا على { يقضى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their torment is never eased; whenever the Fire subsides, its blaze increases.
rows.anchor: بل كلما خبت زيد إسعارها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every kāfūr is excessive in disbelief or ingratitude.
rows.anchor: مبالغ في الكفر أو الكفران

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads the verb passively, making “every unbeliever” its subject; another variant reads يُجازى.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو «يجزى» على بناء المفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reviving the dead means resurrection, or guiding ignorant people.
rows.anchor: الأموات بالبعث أو الجهال بالهداية.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What people sent ahead comprises their past good and evil deeds.
rows.anchor: ما أسلفوا من الأعمال الصالحة والطالحة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Good traces include knowledge taught and an endowment established; bad traces include spreading falsehood and founding injustice.
rows.anchor: الحسنة كعلم علموه وحبيس وقفوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clear register listing everything is the Preserved Tablet.
rows.anchor: فى إمام مبين } يعني اللوح المحفوظ.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Set forth for them” means make an example; the verb takes two objects because it includes “make,” with an annexed noun omitted in “an example like the people of the town.”
rows.anchor: ومثل لهم من قولهم هذه الأشياء على ضرب واحد أي مثال واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the verb may take one expressed object, with the other understood as an appositive or explanatory substitute.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يقتصر على واحد ويجعل المقدر بدلا من الملفوظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The town whose people are the example is Antioch.
rows.anchor: والقرية انطاكية. { إذ جاءها المرسلون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “when the messengers came” clause is an apposition to “the people of the town.”
rows.anchor: إذ جاءها المرسلون } بدل من أصحاب القرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These messengers are Jesus’ apostles sent to the people of Antioch; the wording attributes them to Jesus.
rows.anchor: رسل عيسى عليه الصلاة والسلام إلى أهلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God determined the moon’s course, or its course through stages.
rows.anchor: قدرنا مسيره. { منازل } أو سيره في منازل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The moon passes through 28 mansions, one each night without skipping or falling short; at its final station before conjunction it becomes thin and crooked.
rows.anchor: ينزل كل ليلة في واحد منها لا يتخطاه ولا يتقاصر عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bayḍāwī lists 28 mansions: Cancer, al-Buṭayn, Pleiades, al-Dabarān, al-Haqʿa, al-Hanʿa, al-Dhirāʿ, al-Nathra, al-Ṭarf, al-Jabha, al-Zubra, al-Ṣarfa, al-ʿAwwā, al-Simāk, al-Ghafr, al-Zubānā, al-Iklīl, al-Qalb, al-Shawla, al-Naʿāʾim, al-Balda, Saʿd al-Dhābiḥ, Saʿd Bulaʿ, Saʿd al-Suʿūd, Saʿd al-Akhbiya, Fargh al-Dalw al-Muqaddam, Fargh al-Dalw al-Muʾakhkhar, and al-Rishāʾ.
rows.anchor: وهي ثمانية وعشرون: السرطان، البطين، الثريا، الدبران، الهقعة

rows.speaker: الكوفيون وابن عامر
rows.claim: The Kufans and Ibn ʿĀmir read al-qamar in the accusative.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الكوفيون وابن عامر { والقمر } بنصب الراء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An ʿurjūn is a bent palm shoot; the word is on faʿlūn from inʿirāj, curvature.
rows.anchor: كالشمراخ المعوج، فعلون من الانعراج وهو الاعوجاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Two vocalizations are dialect forms, like two forms of bizyūn.
rows.anchor: وقرىء { كالعرجون } وهما لغتان كالبزيون والبزيون.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Old” means aged; alternatively it means a thing on which a year or more has passed.
rows.anchor: القديم } العتيق وقيل ما مر عليه حول فصاعدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warner is the Qur’an or Messenger; the second-person reading supports the latter.
rows.anchor: القرآن أو الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: نافع وابن عامر ويعقوب
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir, and Yaʿqūb read the verb with تاء.
rows.anchor: قراءة نافع وابن عامر ويعقوب بالتاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Alive” means rational and discerning, since the heedless are dead, or a believer in God’s knowledge, since eternal life comes through faith; warning targets beneficiaries.
rows.anchor: فإن الغافل كالميت، أو مؤمنا في علم الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The binding statement is the sentence of punishment.
rows.anchor: ويحق القول } وتجب كلمة العذاب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unbelievers persist in disbelief; their opposition to the living implies they are truly dead for lack of proof and reflection.
rows.anchor: المصرين على الكفر، وجعلهم في مقابلة من كان حيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Our hands made” means what God alone brought into being; mentioning hands and their work emphasizes exclusive creation.
rows.anchor: مما تولينا إحداثه ولم يقدر على إحداثه غيرنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Livestock are singled out for their remarkable natural features and many benefits.
rows.anchor: خصها بالذكر لما فيها من بدائع الفطرة وكثرة المنافع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People own livestock by God’s grant, or can restrain and manage them because God subjects them.
rows.anchor: متملكون لها بتمليكنا إياها، أو متمكنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unidentified poet uses control of a camel’s head to illustrate milk as ability to restrain something.
rows.anchor: أملك رأس البعير إن نفرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He looked out toward them.
rows.anchor: فأطلع } عليهم. { فرءاه }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person seen is the speaker’s companion.
rows.anchor: { فرءاه } أي قرينه. { فى سواء الجحيم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The companion was in Hell’s middle.
rows.anchor: أي قرينه. { فى سواء الجحيم } وسطه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The companion nearly destroyed the speaker by leading him astray.
rows.anchor: تالله إن كدت لتردين } لتهلكني بالإغواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reads لتغوين; إن is lightened and the lām distinguishes it from إنّ.
rows.anchor: وقرىء «لتغوين» و { إن } هي المخففة واللام هي الفارقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Lord’s favor was guidance and protection.
rows.anchor: ولولا نعمة ربي } بالهداية والعصمة. { لكنت من المحضرين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without that favor, the speaker would have been brought to Hell with his companion.
rows.anchor: لكنت من المحضرين } معك فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This follows an omitted question: “Are we immortal and blessed, so that we will not die?”
rows.anchor: عطف على محذوف أي أنحن مخلدون منعمون فما نحن بميتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reads بمائتين.
rows.anchor: فما نحن بميتين، أي بمن شأنه الموت وقرىء «بمائتين».

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first death includes death in the grave after revival for questioning; it is an accusative cognate object or disconnected exception.
rows.anchor: التي كانت في الدنيا وهي متناولة لما في القبر بعد الإحياء للسؤال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement may rebuke the companion, resume conversation with companions to recount God’s favor, or express boastful wonder and indirect reproach.
rows.anchor: وذلك تمام كلامه لقرينه تقريعا له أو معاودة إلى مكالمة جلسائه تحدثا بنعمة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reads the nūn in Yūnus with kasra.
rows.anchor: { وإن يونس لمن المرسلين } وقرىء بكسر النون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abaqa means fled; though originally used for a slave escaping a master, it fits Jonah leaving without his Lord’s permission.
rows.anchor: هرب، وأصله الهرب من السيد لكن لما كان هربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ship was full.
rows.anchor: إلى الفلك المشحون } المملوء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They cast lots among the ship’s passengers.
rows.anchor: فقارع أهله. { فكان من المدحضين } فصار من المغلوبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jonah lost the drawing; the root image is slipping from a position of victory.
rows.anchor: فصار من المغلوبين بالقرعة، وأصله المزلق عن مقام الظفر.

rows.speaker: روي
rows.claim: A report says Jonah left before God ordered him, boarded a ship that stopped, was identified as a fugitive, lost the lots, admitted fleeing, and threw himself into the water.
rows.anchor: روي أنه لما وعد قومه بالعذاب خرج من بينهم قبل أن يأمره الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fish swallowed Jonah like a morsel in one gulp.
rows.anchor: { فالتقمه الحوت } فابتلعه من اللقمة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mulīm may mean subject to blame, doing something blameworthy, or blaming himself.
rows.anchor: داخل في الملامة، أو آت بما يلام عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant puts fatḥa on mīm and derives it from līma.
rows.anchor: وقرىء بالفتح مبنيا من ليم كمشيب في مشوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jonah praised God throughout life, or in the fish by reciting the prayer in 21:87; another view means he prayed.
rows.anchor: الذاكرين الله كثيرا بالتسبيح مدة عمره، أو في بطن الحوت وهو قوله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative understands “the glorifiers” as people who pray.
rows.anchor: إني كنت من الظلمين [الأنبياء: 87] وقيل من المصلين

words: للبث في بطنه إلى يوم يبعثون
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fish would have kept Jonah inside until the Resurrection, alive or dead.
rows.anchor: للبث فى بطنه إلى يوم يبعثون } حيا وقيل ميتا

words: للبث في بطنه إلى يوم يبعثون
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The episode urges abundant remembrance of God and magnifies its importance.
rows.anchor: وفيه حث على إكثار الذكر وتعظيم لشأنه

words: للبث في بطنه إلى يوم يبعثون
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever turns to God in prosperity is helped by Him in adversity.
rows.anchor: ومن أقبل عليه في السر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God caused the fish to cast Jonah out by its expulsion.
rows.anchor: بأن حملنا الحوت على لفظه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿarāʾ is open ground without tree or plant covering it.
rows.anchor: بالمكان الخالي غما يغطيه من شجر أو نبت

rows.speaker: روي
rows.claim: A report says the fish traveled beside the ship with head raised, Jonah breathing and praising God inside, then cast him ashore.
rows.anchor: روي أن الحوت سار مع السفينة رافعا رأسه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Reports differ on Jonah’s time inside: part of a day, three, seven, twenty, or forty days.
rows.anchor: واختلف في مدة لبثه فقيل بعض يوم وقيل ثلاثة أيام وقيل سبعة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One report says Jonah’s body became like a newborn child’s.
rows.anchor: قيل صار بدنه كبدن الطفل حين يولد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yaqṭīn spreads along the ground without a stalk; its name is linked to settling in a place.
rows.anchor: من شجر ينبسط على وجه الأرض ولا يقوم على ساقه

rows.speaker: الأكثر
rows.claim: Most identify it as a gourd; leaves covered Jonah and kept flies from landing on him.
rows.anchor: والأكثر على أنها كانت الدباء غطته بأوراقها عن الذباب

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: When told he loved gourds, the Prophet agreed and called it “the tree of my brother Jonah.”
rows.anchor: قيل لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: إنك لتحب القرع، قال: " أجل هي شجرة أخي يونس "

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Other views identify the plant as fig or banana; leaves and branches gave shade, and Jonah ate its fruit.
rows.anchor: وقيل التين وقيل الموز تغطى بورقه واستظل بأغصانه

words: لهم من فوقهم ظلل من النار
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Layers of fire above and below explain the unbelievers’ loss; lower layers serve as ceilings for others.
rows.anchor: لهم من فوقهم ظلل من النار } شرح لخسرانهم. { ومن تحتهم ظلل } أطباق من النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God warns with this torment so servants avoid what brings it.
rows.anchor: ذلك العذاب هو الذي يخوفهم به ليتجنبوا ما يوقعهم فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning calls God’s servants to fear Him and avoid what incurs His anger.
rows.anchor: { يا عباد فاتقون } ولا تتعرضوا لما يوجب سخطي.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭāghūt derives from ṭughyān in an emphatic verbal pattern, then serves as an emphatic epithet used particularly of Satan.
rows.anchor: البالغ غاية الطغيان فعلوت منه بتقديم اللام على العين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “That they worship it” is an apposition of inclusion to ṭāghūt.
rows.anchor: { أن يعبدوها } بدل اشتمال منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They turn wholly to God, away from everything else.
rows.anchor: وأقبلوا إليه بشراشرهم عما سواه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their reward is announced by messengers or angels at death.
rows.anchor: بالثواب على ألسنة الرسل، أو الملائكة عند حضور الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explicit description replaces a pronoun for those shunning ṭāghūt, showing their discernment of truth and preference for better courses.
rows.anchor: وضع فيه الظاهر موضع ضمير { الذين اجتنبوا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God guides them to His religion; guidance comes through God’s act and the soul’s acceptance.
rows.anchor: أولئك الذين هداهم الله } لدينه. { وأولئك هم أولوا الألبب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sound minds are free of the competing influence of fancy and habit.
rows.anchor: العقول السليمة عن منازعة الوهم والعادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sent the Book for people’s benefit in worldly and afterlife affairs.
rows.anchor: لأجلهم فإنه مناط مصالحهم في معاشهم ومعادهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Book was sent clothed in truth.
rows.anchor: { بالحق } متلبسا به

words: فمن اهتدى فلنفسه ومن ضل فإنما يضل عليها
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance benefits its follower, while error harms only that person.
rows.anchor: { فمن اهتدى فلنفسه } إذ نفع به نفسه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet was not commissioned to force guidance; he was charged to convey, and conveyed.
rows.anchor: وما وكلت عليهم لتجبرهم على الهدى وإنما أمرت بالبلاغ وقد بلغت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God takes souls by cutting their connection to and control of bodies, wholly inwardly and outwardly in death, but only outwardly during sleep.
rows.anchor: بأن يقطع تعلقها عنها وتصرفها فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God keeps the soul destined for death and does not return it to its body.
rows.anchor: فيمسك التي قضى عليها الموت } ولا يردها إلى البدن،

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read قُضِيَ passively and al-mawt in the nominative.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي قضي بضم القاف وكسر الضاد والموت بالرفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sleeping soul returns to its body on waking, until its appointed death.
rows.anchor: أي النائمة إلى بدنها عند اليقظة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the nafs is for reason and discernment and rūḥ for life, like sun rays in relation; both are taken at death, only the nafs in sleep, close to Bayḍāwī’s account.
rows.anchor: وما روي عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما: أن في ابن آدم نفسا وروحا

words: إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يتفكرون
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Soul-taking, retention, and return show God’s power, wisdom, and mercy; reflection considers body relation, persistence, happiness or misery, and return until death.
rows.anchor: دالة على كمال قدرته وحكمته وشمول رحمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means punishment for evil acts, or recompense for acts generally, called evil because it matches their wrongdoing and hints all their acts were evil.
rows.anchor: جزاء سيئات أعمالهم أو جزاء أعمالهم، وسماه سيئة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who did wrong are defiant among these polytheists; من is explanatory or partitive.
rows.anchor: بالعتو. { من هؤلاء } المشركين و { من } للبيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same consequences struck them: a seven-year drought and their leaders killed at Badr.
rows.anchor: كما أصاب أولئك، وقد أصابهم فإنهم قحطوا سبع سنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They cannot escape God’s punishment.
rows.anchor: وما هم بمعجزين } بفائتين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God withheld provision for seven years, then expanded it for seven years, showing His control.
rows.anchor: حيث حبس عنهم الرزق سبعا ثم بسط لهم سبعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers know all events come from God, directly or through an intermediary.
rows.anchor: بأن الحوادث كلها من الله بوسط أو غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “My servants” refers in Qur’anic usage to believers; they exceeded bounds through sins harming themselves.
rows.anchor: أفرطوا في الجناية عليها بالإسراف في المعاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not despair first of forgiveness, then of God’s further favor.
rows.anchor: لا تيأسوا من مغفرته أولا وتفضله ثانيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God can freely forgive every sin, even after delay; restricting the promise to repentance conflicts with its surface, while 4:48 excludes associating partners.
rows.anchor: عفوا ولو بعد بعد، تقييده بالتوبة خلاف الظاهر

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: A report says that when a man asks whether forgiveness includes one who associated partners, the Prophet replies three times that it does.
rows.anchor: عليه الصلاة والسلام قال " ما أحب أن تكون لي الدنيا وما فيها بها،

rows.speaker: أهل مكة
rows.claim: The verse reportedly followed Meccans’ objection that they worshipped idols and killed unlawfully and wondered how they could emigrate if such sins were unforgiven.
rows.anchor: وما روي أن أهل مكة قالوا: يزعم محمد أن من عبد الوثن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other occasions name ʿAyyāsh, al-Walīd b. al-Walīd, and a tempted group, or al-Waḥshī; these do not narrow the promise.
rows.anchor: وقيل في عياش والوليد بن الوليد في جماعة افتتنوا أو في الوحشي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Emphatic wording conveys exclusivity and mercy after forgiveness; “all” stresses generality, while God’s name evokes His sufficiency and beneficence.
rows.anchor: على المبالغة وإفادة الحصر والوعد بالرحمة بعد المغفرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The possessive address and mention of self-inflicted harm evoke compassion, along with the prohibition on despair and general promise of forgiveness.
rows.anchor: وتقديم ما يستدعي عموم المغفرة مما في { عبادي } من الدلالة على الذلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turn back to God and surrender sincerely before punishment; the command shows the prior promise does not mean forgiveness without repentance or prior punishment.
rows.anchor: بأنها لا تدل على حصول المغفرة لكل أحد من غير توبة

words: واتبعوا أحسن ما أنزل إليكم من ربكم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The best revelation means Qur’an, commanded rather than prohibited matters, decisive rulings rather than concessions, abrogating rather than abrogated material, or the safest and most salvific course.
rows.anchor: القرآن أو المأمور به دون المنهي عنه، والعزائم دون الرخص

words: من قبل أن يأتيكم العذاب بغتة وأنتم لا تشعرون
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Act before punishment comes suddenly without noticing its approach, while time remains to recover.
rows.anchor: وأنتم لا تشعرون } بمجيئه فتتداركوا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means “lest a soul say”; نفس is indefinite because the speaker is one of some souls or to indicate abundance, as in al-Aʿshā’s verse.
rows.anchor: كراهة أن تقول وتنكير { نفس } لأن القائل بعض الأنفس

rows.speaker: الأعشى
rows.claim: Al-Aʿshā’s line illustrates the rhetorical use of an indefinite noun for an individual or abundance.
rows.anchor: كقول الأعشى: ورب بقيع لو هتفت بجوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant retains the original final yāʾ in “my regret.”
rows.anchor: { يا حسرتى } وقرىء بالياء على الأصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The regret is for what the person neglected or fell short in doing.
rows.anchor: { على ما فرطت } بما قصرت.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s “side” means His claim or right, namely obedience; alternatives take it as His essence with an omitted annexed word or His nearness as in 4:36; a reading says remembrance of God.
rows.anchor: في جانبه أي في حقه وهو طاعته

rows.speaker: سابق البربري
rows.claim: Sābiq al-Barbarī’s verse is evidence for جنب meaning a loved one’s right or claim.
rows.anchor: قال سابق البربري: أما تتقين الله في جنب وامق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression is a forceful allusion, like placing generosity and nobility within a dome built over a man.
rows.anchor: وهو كناية فيها مبالغة كقوله: إن السماحة والمروءة والندى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause is accusative as a circumstantial statement: the speaker neglected God’s right while mocking.
rows.anchor: ومحل { إن كنت } نصب على الحال كأنه قال فرطت وأنا ساخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speaker imagines that, had God guided him to truth, he would have avoided shirk and sin.
rows.anchor: بالإرشاد إلى الحق. { لكنت من المتقين } الشرك والمعاصي

words: لو أن لي كرة فأكون من المحسنين
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On seeing punishment, the speaker wishes to return and become good in belief and conduct; the alternatives show futile vacillation and excuses.
rows.anchor: في العقيدة والعمل، وأو للدلالة على أنها لا تخلوا من هذه الأقوال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s response rejects the denial implied by the soul’s claim that God did not guide it.
rows.anchor: رد من الله عليه لما تضمنه قوله { لو أن الله هداني } من معنى النفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reply follows regret, excuse about guidance, then wish to return; inserting it earlier disrupts that sequence.
rows.anchor: لأنه يتحسر بالتفريط ثم يتعلل بفقد الهداية ثم يتمنى الرجعة

words: بلى قد جاءتك آياتي فكذبت بها واستكبرت
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reply neither denies God’s power affecting human action nor attribution of the act to the servant.
rows.anchor: وهو لا يمنع تأثير قدرة الله في فعل العبد ولا ما فيه من إسناد الفعل إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address is masculine according to meaning; a variant uses feminine agreement for نفس.
rows.anchor: وتذكير الخطاب على المعنى، وقرىء بالتأنيث للنفس

words: إن الساعة لآتية لا ريب فيها
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hour will come beyond doubt: its possibility is clear and the messengers unanimously promised it.
rows.anchor: لوضوح الدلالة على جوازها وإجماع الرسل على الوعد بوقوعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most people disbelieve because their thinking is confined to sensory appearances.
rows.anchor: لا يصدقون بها لقصور نظرهم على ظاهر ما يحسون به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Call upon Me” means worship Me; alternatively petition, with refusal to ask treated as refusal to worship, or prayer as a form of worship.
rows.anchor: وقال ربكم ادعونى } اعبدوني. { أستجب لكم } أثبكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s response to the call means that He rewards the worshipper.
rows.anchor: { أستجب لكم } أثبكم لقوله

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو بكر
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr and Abū Bakr read with ḍamma on yāʾ and fatḥa on khāʾ, the passive.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو بكر «سيدخلون» بضم الياء وفتح الخاء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night permits rest because God made it cool and dark, weakening movement and stilling the senses.
rows.anchor: لتستريحوا فيه بأن خلقه باردا مظلما ليؤدي إلى ضعف الحركات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Day is a time or means of seeing; attributing sight to it metaphorically emphasizes the point, phrased as a state rather than purpose.
rows.anchor: يبصر فيه أو به، وإسناد الإبصار إليه مجاز فيه مبالغة

words: إن الله لذو فضل على الناس
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s bounty has no equal; the wording avoids calling Him merely a benefactor, emphasizing its magnitude.
rows.anchor: لا يوازيه فضل، وللإشعار به لم يقل لمفضل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People fail to thank God from ignorance of the giver and neglect of blessings; repeating “people” specifies ingratitude.
rows.anchor: لجهلهم بالمنعم وإغفالهم مواقع النعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those with God are the angels.
rows.anchor: فالذين عند ربك } من الملائكة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels glorify God constantly, as shown by the statement they do not tire.
rows.anchor: يسبحون له بالليل والنهار } أي دائما لقوله: { وهم لا يسئمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth is dry and low-lying; “humble” is borrowed from submission.
rows.anchor: يابسة متطامنة مستعار من الخشوع بمعنى التذلل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After rain, the earth is adorned with growth and swells.
rows.anchor: تزخرفت وانتفخت بالنبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reads ربأت, meaning rose or increased.
rows.anchor: وقرىء «ربأت» أي زادت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The One reviving the dead earth will revive the dead and can do everything, including give life and death.
rows.anchor: بعد موتها. { لمحى الموتى إنه على كل شىء قدير } من الإحياء والإماتة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those deviating from God’s signs attack, falsify, impose false interpretations, or disregard them.
rows.anchor: يميلون عن الاستقامة. { في ءاياتنا } بالطعن والتحريف والتأويل الباطل والإلغاء فيها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their evasions are not hidden from God, who will punish them.
rows.anchor: لا يخفون علينا } فنجازيهم على إلحادهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Contrasting being cast into the Fire with arriving safe on Judgment Day emphatically praises believers’ state.
rows.anchor: قابل الإلقاء في النار بالإتيان آمنا مبالغة في إحماد حال المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Do as you please” is a severe threat; God sees deeds and warns of requital.
rows.anchor: اعملوا ما شئتم } تهديد شديد. { إنه بما تعملون بصير } وعيد بالمجازاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God holds the keys, meaning treasuries, of the heavens and earth.
rows.anchor: له مقاليد السموات والأرض } خزائنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He expands or constricts provision according to His will.
rows.anchor: يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء ويقدر } يوسع ويضيق على وقف مشيئته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows everything and therefore acts fittingly.
rows.anchor: إنه بكل شىء عليم } فيفعله على ما ينبغي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God prescribed the shared religion of Noah, Muhammad, and the other law-bearing prophets.
rows.anchor: أي شرع لكم من الدين دين نوح ومحمد عليهما الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common foundation is establishing religion through required belief and obedience to God’s rulings.
rows.anchor: وهو الأصل المشترك فيما بينهم المفسر بقوله: { أن أقيموا الدين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause may be accusative as apposition to the object of “prescribed,” nominative as an independent answer, or genitive as apposition to the pronoun in به.
rows.anchor: ومحله النصب على البدل من مفعول { شرع } ، أو الرفع على الاستئناف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Communities must not divide over this shared foundation, though branches of law differ, as 5:48 says.
rows.anchor: ولا تختلفوا في هذا الأصل أما فروع الشرائع مختلفة كما قال

words: كبر على المشركين ما تدعوهم إليه
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s call to monotheism is grievous to polytheists.
rows.anchor: { كبر على المشركين } عظم عليهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yajtabī means God draws people to Him; the pronoun refers to the call or religion.
rows.anchor: يجتلب إليه والضمير لما تدعوهم أو للدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God guides by indication and enabling those who turn to Him.
rows.anchor: بالإشارة والتوفيق
